cards.front: State the Squeeze Theorem for sequences.
cards.back: If there exists N such that for all n ≥ N we have a_n ≤ b_n ≤ c_n, and lim a_n = lim c_n = L (finite), then lim b_n = L.

cards.front: What must hold for the bounding sequences in the Squeeze Theorem?
cards.back: a_n and c_n must both converge to the same finite limit L; the inequality a_n ≤ b_n ≤ c_n must hold for all sufficiently large n.

cards.front: Apply the Squeeze Theorem to evaluate lim (n→∞) (sin n)/n.
cards.back: -1 ≤ sin n ≤ 1 implies -1/n ≤ (sin n)/n ≤ 1/n for n > 0. Both -1/n → 0 and 1/n → 0, hence lim (sin n)/n = 0.

cards.front: If |a_n| ≤ b_n and lim b_n = 0, what is lim a_n?
cards.back: -b_n ≤ a_n ≤ b_n and both -b_n, b_n → 0, so by Squeeze Theorem lim a_n = 0.

cards.front: Prove the Squeeze Theorem for sequences.
cards.back: Let ε > 0. ∃N₁ s.t. n > N₁ ⇒ |a_n - L| < ε; ∃N₂ s.t. n > N₂ ⇒ |c_n - L| < ε. Let N = max(N₁, N₂, N₀) where N₀ makes a_n ≤ b_n ≤ c_n true. Then L - ε < a_n ≤ b_n ≤ c_n < L + ε, so |b_n - L| < ε.

cards.front: Why does the Squeeze Theorem fail if lim a_n ≠ lim c_n?
cards.back: The hypothesis requires both outer limits to equal the same L; otherwise b_n may oscillate or diverge between two different limits.

cards.front: Give a sequence squeezed to 0 whose terms are not eventually positive.
cards.back: a_n = (-1)^n / n. Then -1/n ≤ a_n ≤ 1/n and both bounds → 0, so a_n → 0 despite sign changes.
